grades.reason: General overview of the LoongArch ISA and its components. It doesn't mention data-access ordering or instruction-fetch synchronization instructions.
Only says which floating-point instructions apply to LA32 and LA64. It has nothing about barriers or instruction-fetch synchronization.

grades.quote: In addition to the above atomic sequence of operations, the `AM{SWAP/ADD}_DB.{B/H}` instruction also implements the data barrier function.
grades.reason: Says the _DB variants of the AM atomic instructions also act as data barriers, ordering earlier and later memory accesses on the same core. That partly answers the data-ordering half. It doesn't cover the dedicated barrier instructions (DBAR) or any instruction-fetch synchronization (IBAR).
